rules: Successor raster IRQ selection uses logical line 128 after display setup at initial and resumed entry. This is above all six-bit RASLINE0 starts and below both PAL/NTSC maxima including optional one-line delay. Preserve D011 display bits; no timing-source or IRQ-handler change. Diagnostic bytes 100-107 sample CPU P, D019, D01A, D06F, D079, D07A and the CPU-visible vector after the resumed interval and before cleanup. These are sequential observations, not an atomic hardware snapshot; 255 means not reached. No diagnostic reading can replace real IRQ-count advancement.
The storage boundary occurs after a complete authoritative tick and before the next tick release.
No authoritative tick advances while the lifecycle is QUIESCED through APPLICATION_RESTORED.
The same model object, RNG/checksum lineage and snapshot owner state continue after storage.
Application DMA is synchronous and empty before KERNAL ownership.
VIC-IV display fetch is suspended after renderer drain and before ROM restoration, then resumed only after application and canonical platform restoration.
Display, audio, input, IRQ and DMA service paths all execute again after SERVICES_RESUMED.

Before successor ROM-protection toggles, release CIA2 ATN/CLK/DATA only outside KERNAL transactions, preserve bank bits and DDRs, and refuse CIA1 serial-output ownership. Never write D67D or reset a hardware-IEC controller from user mode. The existing real IRQ advancement requirement remains the pass criterion; returned feature bits are diagnostic, since Xemu does not model IEC/defer semantics.

IRQ_BEFORE and IRQ_AFTER are coherent PF001 seqlock snapshots around only the resumed tick interval; nonzero modular count advancement is required. IEC_OUTPUT_BEFORE, IEC_OUTPUT_RELEASED and RECLAIM_FEATURES retain the post-storage port-output bits read, released value written, and trap return byte; 255 means not reached.
The sticky NMI observation is recorded and invalidates the run before, during or after storage, including resumed authoritative ticks and final completion.
A failed post-storage tick preserves its first recorded fault; code 87 is used only when no inner fault was recorded.
Any lifecycle, snapshot, ROM, storage, canonical-state, reserve, NMI or continuation failure enters permanent lockout.
The T02 ranges, public ABI, high-level map, 100 Hz release and 21-stage order remain unchanged.
